en: For the marketplace held fast and closed,
His fortune differs from all other people's.
He brings great devastation upon the enemy.
Let me tell you, bold one, what there is for you.
Perhaps you have already heard:
At the edge of Janjurbos,
Her waist slender as a sheath, her face moonlike,
I saw a fairy-born maiden.
Akbermet, the daughter of a peri,
I saw her form and admired it.
A great beauty born of the peri,
Serenely radiant with wondrous light.
Taste the sugar, then hear her words.
Mortals melt without even realizing it.
She moves languidly, swaying as she walks.
Finds the mortal heart distracted.
She has grown into a swaying, graceful woman,
She walks serenely, turning gracefully,
She walks in radiance, moving gracefully,
Anyone who sees her appearance from afar,
When she emerges from the steep bank,
Ah, when snow falls upon the dark earth,
See her skin, whiter than that snow.
If snow falls upon this snow,
See the girl's face, like that snow.
Look at her finely proportioned form.
Her voice is sweet as a nightingale's.
Those who see her cannot contain themselves.
From a hollow in the mountain's spur,
Beside the tall poplar,
She seized the lead rope and cried out,
Sobbing with all her strength,
You entrusted many messages to me.
You have courage; quiet your restless heart.
Akbermet spoke a word,
The unfortunate daughter of a peri,
Grasping the lead rope and crying out,
Weeping in earnest, sobbing bitterly,
Stay a moment there before me,
My beloved holy man.
I have a wondrous voice full of melody.
Has been consumed by love's unfolding.
Has spoiled and stripped away my complexion.
It has left this unfortunate soul grieving.
The moon waned and days passed,
Many years went by in between,
My mind was filled with bewilderment.
When my father had grown old,
He slaughtered many animals for the celebration,
He called me his child and found contentment.
From my first year he indulged me,
From the age of seven, dear mother,
With my head turned toward the qibla,
In a dream while I was sleeping,
His name was Kyzyr.
White Kyzyr, the wandering holy man,
Simply said, take it, and extended his hand.
My wealthy father, who had not noticed,
The holy wanderer named Kyzyr,
Spoke softly, laying firm emphasis,
Beginning a precious saying, asking that it be spoken,
I will tell you a wondrous thing; understand it.
Speaking of such a wondrous heart,
Has sought you, saying he is your bridegroom.
Saying, my wondrous tale has no end,
Is your destined equal, unfortunate girl, he said.
If I speak, my words are fitting, he said.
Is the bridegroom you will willingly marry, he said.
And girded himself with steel without a sheath.
Wrath swept across his face,
Wherever he struck was blazing fire,
Where in this world could his like be found?
When he grew wrathful and exerted strength,
The fearsome youth's black-spotted leopards,
Charged forth on every side,
No mortal could be like him.
This is the lord of splendor.
His whole world is in harmony,
This is the man with whom to explore them.
The Almighty's decree cannot be evaded,
Holding one another in our arms,
Staying together in delight,
When light touched the earth,
My flesh and nails strained,
Consumed by the fire of love,
Thinking I should depart,
Because of love's fire,
No fine steed, no charger to ride,
Hearing he roamed the world,
Finding no way out of it,
I strapped weapons to my body,
Of exceptional valor,
From warriors who drew the bow,
From marksmen who never missed,
From champions peerless with the spear,
I gathered them in a great host,
From champions whose shots never erred,
Because of my unfulfilled desire,
I gathered their steeds.
The four corners of the world,
I traveled around them four times,
I stirred fierce conflict.
Worn down but still alive,
Bringing death to whoever encountered it,
Beyond that,
It had a swordlike snout and tongue,
It had strength to swallow the world,
We found ourselves plunged,
He was a giant too great for the earth,
His dark eyes watching,
Beginning my account plainly,
The terrible ordeal and great conflict,
My priceless golden life.
I [lost] so many of my people,
Meeting and speaking together,
I have lost my senses, dear elder,
[I shall not abandon the one I pursue],
Hoping to open my eyes and see him,
My heart suffered greatly,
I withered yellow as straw, lamenting,
Lamenting, I wandered in distress,
This poor soul burning like flame,
I have yielded to your sorrowful words,
Much lies ahead before you meet him,
He is a lion unlike ordinary men,
Once, beside the Seven Rivers,
These very eyes witnessed it,
“The child will do something extraordinary,”
Taking the form of a hungry lion,
His being born clutching dark blood,
Fighting them,
Listen carefully to this,
Of lionhearted Seitek, the gray wolf,
To the hapless fairy maiden,
The heir left by the dear departed,
Make him understand his ignorance,
The [holy] elder spoke,
Reflecting, he spoke thus,
To the hollow of [Jylgyndy],
Cuckoos calling from [mountain to mountain],
[Nightingales] trilled and chirped.
Akjoltoi arrived.
A roaring, mighty shout,
Setting out in search of a saint,
It would never let the enemy seize him,
From your beloved for all eternity,
Akjoltoi of Kutubiy,
I shall be your inheritance,
Descended from lion-slaying heroes.
Hero, we joined together when thumb-sized.
A star stirred in the heavens.
Becoming a gray horse among white horses,
Who dwelled in the Seven Rivers,
Kyyas of the Jediger,
For Kyyas, the son of Bagysh,
When we brought slaughter to their borders,
The enemy who opposed us,
We leveled with the black earth.
We became friends until Judgment Day.
He was a formidable enemy,
The enemy who fancied himself a gray-maned wolf,
We showed our wolf-like valor,
We openly burned them in the blaze [cancelled: in fire].
Against the enemy who threatened war,
For the Kyrgyz of Talas,
Whatever guilt or merit there may be,
Let us undertake one duty.
At last I could find no peace,
The Kulduu Badam armor no bullet pierces,
If they fought face to face.
Firing guns and drawing bows,
If they stood striking with thudding blows.
The Kulduu Badam armor no bullet pierces,
[Cancelled: Forty] the forty tribes of Kara-Kytai,
Beyond the ridge are the Chinese,
Before you are the Barang,
One granted exceptional honor,
From your tiger forefather Manas,
Wishing to serve before you,
Has renounced and abandoned it.
[Cancelled: Despairing of life,]
If she does not see you,
So that longing for you might seize her.
As recited by Sayakbai Karalaev
The epic of Seitek
These are the words spoken by Akjoltoi.
If his world is whole and prosperous,
If his heart is as broad as a lake,
That unfortunate peri-born woman,
Of one lineage and shared blood,
Accept it with blessing.
Lend your ear to these words,
This world is full of delight,
Immerse yourself in its pleasures,
Your heroism is exceptional,
To you, whom Khyzyr has blessed,
She came as your good fortune,
From his father back to his forefathers,
Through his descendants and lineage,
Accept your horse like Kulan-Sur,
Take me myself, your irreplaceable inheritance,
If an enemy comes surging against you,
I too shall turn and thrust my spear.
I shall serve without turning aside.
If there are blackening, burning embers,
Without stirring to flee death,
I too shall stand beneath the banner,
I am your inexhaustible travel food.
[When you need me at your side,]
Come forth across its path,
I shall wield your sword.
Draped that coat of mail about him,
Raged like a blue-gray tiger.
Wisdom came from the unseen,
So I might drive back foes without tiring,
Made the place of combat run with blood,
Thus you brought me understanding,
My falcon inherited from the noble hawk,
Joiner of what was severed,
Born in Jeti-Suu,
Let us choose the swiftest mounts.
Let us crush them and scatter their blood,
Scatter their turmoil to dust,
Here am I, your lion Seytek,
My equal, that fairy’s daughter,
Spoke these words distinctly,
If she makes a gate for my city,
Without causing me sorrow,
He spoke quietly, leaving firm words,
Warrior Akjoltoy began to speak,
Of that hapless fairy-born maiden,
Taking a thousand fairy troops,
She shattered her firm fortune,
She had her champions slaughtered,
She brought her poor soul to exhaustion,
Crushing it into a fur cap,
Her love became apparent,
She began a momentous quarrel.
She abandoned her possessions.
Tears poured from her eyes,
There he pitched his white royal tent,
Her road-scouting guide,
[An enchanter and sorcerer,]
She abandoned it all and hurried.
For your sake, my leopard hero,
Her fragile soul cries out,
She truly bursts into tears,
Slaughter ninety beasts for her wedding,
Let her be named Bermet.
Let us go out to meet her.
Let envious enemies rejoice.
The tiger among the twelve,
Who truly knew his secrets,
He attacked the enemy without tiring,
Riding out on reconnaissance,
Told to spill blood, they unleashed their fury,
